statement: A news website surveyed $250$ readers about their age group and where they get most of their news. $$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \text{Online} & \text{TV} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Under } 30 & 62 & 18 & 80 \\ 30 \text{ to } 50 & 49 & 41 & 90 \\ \text{Over } 50 & 21 & 59 & 80 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 132 & 118 & 250 \end{array}$$ A reader who gets most news from TV is chosen at random. What is the probability that this reader is over $50$?

choices.misconception: I divided 59 by all 250 readers, but the reader is chosen only from the 118 TV readers.
I found the share of all readers who are over 50, 80 out of 250, and never used the TV condition.
I divided by the 80 readers over 50, which gives the chance that an over-50 reader prefers TV, the reverse of what was asked.

hints: The reader is chosen only from those who prefer TV. Which total goes in the denominator?
Use the TV column. Divide the over-$50$ count in that column by the TV total.
The TV column total is $118$ and the over-$50$ entry is $59$.

solutions.reliable: The reader is chosen from the $118$ TV readers. Of those, $59$ are over $50$. The probability is $\dfrac{59}{118} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
